entries.action: Mechanism-relative channel rule for R-BODY-1/2 (behind P1): test any channel-interaction proposal PER BODY, never in general — controlled-ridge gains do not transfer to neural bodies. Keep the frozen-body + post-hoc-support SHAPE (bounded support atop frozen CI forecaster wins 12/16): it is our B3-instrument pattern, independently validated. Third vindication of ridge-first methodology (controlled ridge reveals what neural nets hide).
entries.note: Related ≠ useful ≠ used: dependency structures shift across horizons; horizon-adaptive source selection helps a controlled ridge in 21/32 conditions (+5.16% mean, transfers to matched nonlinear), but the same logic on iTransformer gives 11/20 wins at +0.208% with no alignment to controlled gains. Strong forecasters use cross-channel info yet their source-reliance rankings agree little with controlled utility or across iTransformer/TimesNet/TimeMixer. Bounded post-hoc support improves a frozen channel-independent forecaster in 12/16 conditions (positive aggregate bootstrap).
entries.relevance: R-BODY channel rule: mechanism-relative testing + frozen-body/post-hoc pattern support.
entries.title: Rethinking Cross-Channel Importance in Time-Series Forecasting

entries.action: Pre-registered P1-channel pre-check (behind P1, before any xCPD/Chameleon work): profile OUR 10-indicator set with lagged MI + CD-gain (CD vs CI variant). If CD-gain ≤ 0 on our set, channel-interaction work stays parked — the standard literature datasets are exactly the trap (median CD gain −4.9%, CI wins 10/10 MSE).
entries.note: Standard MTSF datasets mostly lack the coupling CD models assume: median 23% lagged-coupled pairs, median CD gain −4.9%; chaotic ODEs 78%/+4.6%. Only lagged MI and the model-based CD gain (CD vs CI variant) recover all planted couplings (Granger/TE fail). New MixBench-TS (10 real sets, 55.5% coupled, +1.7% CD gain): CI wins 10/10 MSE on standard sets but only 3/10 on MixBench. Recommendation: profile new datasets with lagged MI + CD gain before evaluating multivariate models.
entries.relevance: P1-channel pre-check: measure coupling before modeling it.
entries.title: MixBench-TS: A Multivariate Time Series Forecasting Benchmark Where Channel Mixing Pays Off

entries.action: Memory-architecture direction (dormant — banks live, sharing dead): if memory ever re-opens, the literature-shaped alternative is PARAMETERIZED memory (domain dynamics internalized as learnable latent prototypes, retrieval-free, constant-time), not retrieve-and-share transfer. Converges with P3a from the other side: sharing-style transfer is the wrong shape; internalize or delete.
entries.note: MEMTS: Knowledge Persistence Module internalizes domain temporal dynamics (seasonal patterns, trends) into compact learnable latent prototypes — fragmented history becomes continuous parameterized knowledge. Retrieval-free domain adaptation with constant-time inference, near-zero latency, no catastrophic forgetting of global patterns, no backbone modification. SOTA on multiple datasets. Frames the alternative to RAG-style retrieve-and-share: DAPT forgets, RAG costs, parameterization keeps.
entries.title: MEMTS: Internalizing Domain Knowledge via Parameterized Memory

entries.action: P2-pipeline note (pipeline stands; for any future R-FEAT work): normalization choices have loss-geometry consequences — RevIN inverse-norm injects squared-scale weighting (fix: context-normalized coordinates); shared CD affine preserves candle-order relations that independent transforms break; scale-adaptive stabilization for multi-order-magnitude assets. Our per-feature squash is exactly the independent-transform shape — any R-FEAT proposal must show cross-channel relation preservation.
entries.note: CryptoL (financial MTSF): extreme cross-asset scale heterogeneity + OHLC structural dependencies. Context-normalized error coordinates in RevIN pipeline (prevents inverse-norm squared-scale weighting; formal risk/gradient-geometry characterization of large-scale-asset dominance); shared channel-dependent vs independent normalization (shared CD affine preserves candle-order relations); scale-adaptive stabilization + soft OHLC-inequality feasibility loss. Controlled ablations: better accuracy, stability, and financially-valid OHLC rate.
entries.relevance: R-FEAT constraint: cross-channel relation preservation + scale geometry.
entries.title: CryptoL: Towards Scale Dominance and Physics Constraints Mitigation in Financial MTSF
